A professional racing driver by profession and the first Malaysian from the State of Sarawak to compete in GT cars and LMP3, racing between 2009 and 2021. Over the course of Zen’s career, he has entered 136 races, securing 58 podium finishes and 20 victories before retiring. Born in the State of Kuching to a working-class family, Zen Low began kart racing competitively at the age of 18. However, due to financial limitations, it forced him to stop his kart racing after just one season. In 1995, he began jet ski racing with Team Wong Way Racing, where he became champion in the Novice Runabout Open category of the Malaysian Jet Sports Championship. The following year, he joined Team Petronas Jetsport, achieving 10 podium finishes, out of which six were in the number one spot, and finishing second overall in the championship. By 1998, financial constraints once again brought his racing ambition to a halt. In 2009, Zen Low, still burning with determination and drive in motorsports, transitioned to car racing after securing sufficient funding. He began his GT career with Lotus Cars Malaysia, driving a Lotus Elise Mk1 in the Malaysia Merdeka Endurance Race (MMER) 12 Hours, where he qualified second but luck was not on his side as he did not finish the race due to technical issue. In 2010, Zen competed in the Megalap Time Attack, finishing second in the Supersport Production class, and won the European Car category in the Zerotohundred Time Attack. That same year, he returned to Malaysia Merdeka Endurance Race (MMER) with a Lotus 2-Eleven, this time again qualifying second but retired from the race. In 2011, Zen took part in the Malaysia Super Series race, finishing second overall in a Lotus Exige. But in the MMER 12 Hours race, he qualified second but fate has it that he again did not finish the race. The following year, in 2012, he finally broke the chain of bad fortune and claimed the national championship title in the Malaysia Super Series with seven podium finishes. His success continued in 2013 when he won the Asian Le Mans Series (3 Hours of Sepang) in the GTC category with a Lamborghini Gallardo GT3. He also finished second overall in the Lamborghini Blancpain Super Trofeo Asia Pacific with five podiums and secured second place in the GT4 class at the MMER 12 Hours with a Lotus Evora. In 2014, he was placed third overall in the Lamborghini Blancpain Super Trofeo Asia Pacific, having seven podium finishes. In 2015, Zen finished second overall in the CN class of the Asian Le Mans Series driving a Wolf prototype. He was placed seventh overall in the GT Asia Series driving a Lamborghini Gallardo GT3, and finished seventh overall in the Sepang 12 Hours endurance race with a Lamborghini Huracán GT3. 2016 was a good year for Zen Low. He got second and third position in the Sprint Cup of the Asian Le Mans Series, seventh overall in the Endurance Cup with an LMP3 Ginetta, second overall with eight podiums in the Lamborghini Blancpain Super Trofeo Asia and was crowned the overall GT4 champion for the Sepang 12 Hours with a Ginetta. In 2017, Zen became the first and only Malaysian to be fully sponsored by Ferrari Malaysia to compete in the Ferrari Challenge Asia-Pacific, where he finished third overall with seven podiums. That same year, he competed in the Bathurst 12 Hour endurance race, finishing fourth in the GT4 category. In 2018, he was selected by the Motorsport Association of Malaysia (MAM) to represent the country at the inaugural FIA GT Nations Cup in Bahrain. Team Malaysia finished eighth overall with an Audi R8 GT3. In 2019, Zen secured third overall in the Lamborghini Super Trofeo Asia Pacific championship with seven podium finishes. After the disruption by the COVID-19 pandemic, Zen concluded his racing career in 2021 on a high note by winning the Sepang 1000 km Endurance Race in the Toyota Vios Enduro Cup. From 2022 to 2026, Zen Low has remained active in motorsport as a drifting driver, collaborating with International and local brands such as Monster Energy, Goodyear, Autobacs, Milwaukee, TikTok Malaysia, XPEL, and Carlist. Family Zen Low was born on 12 February 1969 in Kuching, Sarawak, East Malaysia, into a working-class family. His father, Low Ngi Huat, was a businessman in the entertainment industry, while his mother, Then Moi Ing, was a homemaker who also assisted in the family business. He is one of four siblings, with two sisters and one brother. [[User:Kisseran|Kisseran]] ([[User talk:Kisseran|talk]]) 17:14, 10 November 2026 (UTC)}} {{AfC comment|1=In preparing this draft, I disclose that AI assistance was used as follows: {{Hidden begin}}nowiki{{LLM-assisted translation}} {{Short description|French harpsichordist and author (born 1960)}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Olivier Baumont | background = non_vocal_instrumentalist | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1960|8|15|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Saint-Dié-des-Vosges]], France | instrument = [[Harpsichord]] | occupation = Harpsichordist, author, teacher | genre = [[Classical music]], [[Baroque music]] | website = {{URL|https://www.olivierbaumont.fr/}} }} '''Olivier Baumont''' (born 15 August 1960) is a French [[harpsichordist]], author and teacher. His career has focused particularly on French keyboard music of the 17th and 18th centuries. He has taught harpsichord at the [[Conservatoire de Paris]] since 2001 and has recorded the complete harpsichord works of [[François Couperin]], [[Jean-Philippe Rameau]] and [[Jacques Duphly]].<ref name="Larousse">{{cite encyclopedia |title=Olivier Baumont |encyclopedia=Dictionnaire de la musique |publisher=Larousse |url=https://www.larousse.fr/encyclopedie/musdico/Olivier_Baumont/166144 |language=fr }}</ref><ref name="CNSMDP">{{cite web |title=Olivier Baumont |url=https://www.conservatoiredeparis.fr/fr/enseignant/baumont-olivier |website=Conservatoire de Paris |language=fr |access-date=10 November 2026 }}</ref> == Biography == === Early life and education === Born in [[Saint-Dié-des-Vosges]], France, Baumont began studying the harpsichord at the conservatory in [[Annecy]]. He continued his studies at the [[Conservatoire de Paris]], where he obtained first prizes in harpsichord and chamber music in 1981 and 1982. He subsequently studied with [[Huguette Dreyfus]] and [[Kenneth Gilbert]], and attended interpretation classes given by [[Gustav Leonhardt]] in Cologne, Germany.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> In 1982, he won the Radio France soloists' competition and made his first recording.<ref name="Larousse"/> === Musical career === Baumont has performed in recitals and chamber music concerts throughout France and internationally. He has appeared at the Ambronay Festival, the [[Festival de La Roque-d'Anthéron]], the Radio France and Montpellier Festival and events organised by the Centre de musique baroque de Versailles. His performances have also taken him to Japan, the United States, Canada, South America and various European countries.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> In the early 1990s, he became artistic director of the Festival Couperin, originally held in [[Chaumes-en-Brie]] and subsequently in [[Champs-sur-Marne]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Festival Couperin |url=https://www.lexpress.fr/informations/festival-couperin_595850.html |work=L'Express |date=23 September 1993 |language=fr }}</ref> He has collaborated with musicians including [[Davitt Moroney]], [[Jean-Paul Fouchécourt]], [[Hugo Reyne]], [[Christophe Coin]] and [[Julien Chauvin (violinist)|Julien Chauvin]]. In March 2014, Baumont initiated a series at the [[Cité de la musique]] in Paris devoted to the complete harpsichord works of [[Johann Sebastian Bach]]. The project brought together twenty harpsichordists of different generations and featured historical instruments.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> === Teaching and music research === In September 2001, Baumont was appointed professor of harpsichord at the [[Conservatoire de Paris]], where he has also taught continuo playing.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> Alongside his teaching, he gives masterclasses and lectures on historical performance practice and the French Baroque repertoire. His research has included editing and restoring keyboard music by composers such as [[Michel Corrette]], [[Jacques Duphly]] and Francis Thomé. He has also appeared on radio and television programmes devoted to classical music, including broadcasts on [[France Musique]], [[France Culture]], the BBC and Mezzo. === Theatre and cinema === Baumont's work has extended beyond the concert stage to theatre, literature and cinema. He adapted [[Denis Diderot]]'s ''[[Rameau's Nephew]]'' for the theatre. The production was performed in Paris, notably at the Théâtre Le Ranelagh, with actors Nicolas Vaude and Nicolas Marié, before touring. In 2016, he contributed the music for ''[[A Woman's Life (film)|A Woman's Life]]'' (''Une vie''), directed by [[Stéphane Brizé]] and based on the novel by [[Guy de Maupassant]]. The film's music draws in part on 18th-century keyboard works, including compositions by Jacques Duphly.<ref>{{cite web |title=Une vie |url=https://diaphana.fr/film/une-vie/ |website=Diaphana Distribution |language=fr }}</ref> Baumont has also performed with the French actor [[Denis Podalydès]] in literary concerts combining readings and harpsichord music, particularly around the works of [[Marcel Proust]].<ref name="Franciscaines">{{cite web |title=Olivier Baumont |url=https://festivallitterairedeauville.fr/fr/artistes/olivier-baumont |website=Les Franciscaines |language=fr }}</ref> === Recordings === Baumont has recorded a substantial repertoire of Baroque keyboard music. His discography includes the complete harpsichord works of [[Jean-Philippe Rameau]] and [[François Couperin]], as well as recordings devoted to [[Johann Sebastian Bach]], [[Henry Purcell]], [[George Frideric Handel]] and [[Georg Philipp Telemann]]. He has also recorded music by [[Jacques Champion de Chambonnières]], [[Louis-Claude Daquin]], [[Jean-François Dandrieu]] and [[Claude Balbastre]]. In 2022, he released ''Un clavecin pour Marcel Proust'', an album associated with the musical world of the French novelist, marking the centenary of Proust's death. In 2024, Plectra Music released his recording of works by [[Michel Corrette]], entitled ''Les Amants Enchantés & Other Harpsichord Pieces''. In 2026, Baumont released a complete recording of [[Jacques Duphly]]'s harpsichord works on the Plectra Music label. Recorded on historical harpsichords from the Flint Collection in the United States, the three-disc set comprises all 52 of Duphly's harpsichord pieces. The recording was reviewed by François Ekchajzer in ''[[Télérama]]'' in August 2026.<ref name="Duphly2026">{{cite magazine |last=Ekchajzer |first=François |title=Complete Works for Harpsichord : Jacques Duphly d'Olivier Baumont : notre critique |url=https://www.telerama.fr/musique/complete-works-for-harpsichord-jacques-duphly-d-olivier-baumont-notre-critique_cri-7045559.php |magazine=Télérama |date=25 August 2026 |language=fr }}</ref> === Writing and literary activities === In addition to his musical career, Baumont has published several books on French musical history, literature and the relationship between music and the arts. In 1998, he published ''Couperin, le musicien des rois'' in the [[Découvertes Gallimard]] collection. The book received the Prix des Muses that year.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> His 2007 book ''La Musique à Versailles'', published by Actes Sud in collaboration with the Palace of Versailles and the Centre de musique baroque de Versailles, received an award from the French music critics' association.<ref name="CNSMDP"/> He later published ''À l'Opéra, monsieur ! La musique dans les Mémoires de Saint-Simon'' (Gallimard, 2015) and ''Tombeau du jeune monsieur de Cinq-Mars'' (Arléa, 2021). In 2024, he published his first novel, ''D'une partition m'apparaissait un dessin'', with Bleu nuit. The novel was shortlisted for the 2025 Prix Livres & Musiques, awarded at Les Franciscaines in Deauville.<ref name="Franciscaines"/> === Residencies at Chambord === Baumont has maintained an artistic association with the [[Château de Chambord]], where he has performed concerts and undertaken several writing residencies. His first two residencies contributed to the development of ''À l'Opéra, monsieur !'' and ''Tombeau du jeune monsieur de Cinq-Mars''. In 2026, he undertook a third writing residency at Chambord to research a book on the history of music at the château, from the Renaissance to the present day. The project examines the role of music in the château's history, including court entertainments, theatre, religious ceremonies, hunting traditions and later artistic performances.<ref name="Chambord2026">{{cite web |title=Résidence d'artiste – Olivier Baumont |url=https://www.chambord.org/fr/residence-dartiste-olivier-baumont/ |website=Domaine national de Chambord |year=2026 |language=fr |access-date=10 November 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Rencontre hors-les-murs – Artistes en circuit-court – Olivier Baumont |url=https://www.chambord.org/fr/post/rencontres-hors-les-murs-artistes-en-circuit-court-olivier-baumont/ |website=Domaine national de Chambord |year=2026 |language=fr }}</ref> == Publications == * Baumont, Olivier.
